messages:
Anna: Heads-up — ran a perfetto/nsys sweep on staging for the new continuous-batching tweak. Trace attached: link (internal). Observed recurring queue spikes at ~120ms pre-kernel
Josh: Can you paste the summary numbers? queue vs compute breakdown?
Anna: Quick numbers: avg wall time 340ms, queue 140ms, compute 200ms. But when KV cache hits >80% queue drops to ~60ms.
Li: Interesting — kernel selection looks like it's preferring matmul_fused_v2 on long sequences, which increases compute but reduces enqueue churn. Did you capture kernel timelines?
Anna: Yep — perf-bot posted the nsys snippet: [nsys://r/abcd123]. Timeline shows frequent kernel switch at batch boundaries; each switch costs ~10-15ms due to workspace init.
Maya: That workspace init sounds like the kernel reroute penalty we saw in canary. Could batching boundaries be causing extra cold starts because the scheduler reassigns affinity?
Josh: I also noticed a correlation with small batch tails — when continuous window size is 25ms, we get more tiny batches which trigger kernel choice change. Raising window to 40ms reduces switches but ups queue time.
Anna: I tried a run with window=35ms and adaptive affinity disabled: queue 95ms compute 220ms, overall 315ms — slightly better. But KV prefetching seemed to take more host CPU.
Li: Prefetch threads contending with launch threads? Any CPU-side stalls in nsys?
Anna: perf-bot: cpu-time breakdown points to wakeups in prefetcher at ~12% host CPU; nvtx shows stalls when KV miss rate spikes.
Maya: Could we change kernel selection policy to prefer a stable kernel when batch variability high? e.g., stick to matmul_generic if variance > threshold.
Josh: That would increase compute but reduce context switch cost. Need an estimate: if each switch costs 12ms and we avoid 3 switches per second per GPU = 36ms saved.
Anna: Also looked at KV cache sweep behavior — sweep interval 500ms causes batch-boundary-aligned sweeps, leading to synchronized misses. Staggering sweep reduced peak misses in a short run.
Li: Good call — add jitter to sweep timer and test with window=30ms.
perf-bot: nsys report: peak GPU occupancy 64%, avg 58%, kernel-switch events 47 in 120s, KV-miss bursts correlated with sweep timestamp.
Oncall Bot: Note filed: RT-3214 with stack trace and perf artifacts. Assign to eng-runtime perf.
Maya: Next action: run 2x with (window=30,jittered-sweep) and (window=40,sticky-kernel-policy) and compare p50/p95. I'll schedule.
Anna: I'll push the traces and a small script to reproduce the tiny-batch pattern. Thanks :thumbsup:
